archived.title: CLI polish: clap, --help/--version, session-override flags, Windows console attach
archived.description: Make PhotoBlaze a pleasant cross-platform CLI citizen for scripted launches. Today (main.rs:3406-3525): hand-rolled args, no --help/--version, unknown flags silently swallowed; release Windows builds are GUI-subsystem so nothing can print anyway. Decision (owner, 2026-07-11): use clap 4 (derive) - binary cost is a rounding error on this exe, parse time is launch-only, and it buys polished help/typo suggestions/value validation/completions for a low-usage feature. clap lives in pb-app ONLY (pb-app-core stays toml-only per NS0); the CLI parses into a plain LaunchOverrides struct the core consumes. Overrides NEVER persist to settings.toml (a scripted --dark --slideshow=5 launch must not rewrite the user's config).
archived.details:
Order of operations in main(): (1) Velopack --veloapp-* intercept stays FIRST (update.rs:402); (2) Windows: AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) + rebind stdout/stderr BEFORE parsing (clap's help/errors are invisible without it; known cosmetic PowerShell prompt-interleave wart is acceptable); (3) clap parse; (4) launch. Register the hidden dev flags (--hud-gallery, --egui-shot, --settings-shot, --light, --tab, --welcome, --metrics) as hide=true so clap doesn't error on them. Parse-error fallback: no console attached (double-click / file association) -> existing Message dialog instead of a silent exit; console -> normal stderr + exit 2. Flag set (long + short where sensible), all mapping to existing state per the 2026-07-11 survey: --fullscreen/-f, --windowed/-w (exist); --recursive/-r, --no-recursive (exist); --info/--no-info (settings.show_image_info); --details (Panels.inspector, the Shift+I inspector); --folders (folder_tree_open); --slideshow[=SECS] (slideshow + interval); --scale <fit|fill|original> (scale_mode); --theme <light|dark|system> (appearance_mode); --mute (mute_live_audio); --shuffle (NEW small feature: start nav in the precomputed pb-core shuffle order - randomness today is per-keypress, not a mode); --version (build.rs build-id stamp, same string as About). Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 usage/bad path (with stderr message when console attached). Docs: README CLI section; optional clap_complete completions later. Estimate: 1-2 focused days; the AttachConsole shim is the only fiddly part.

RESOLVED DECISIONS (owner Q&A, 2026-07-11, branch feat/cli-clap): (a) STRICTNESS = Mixed - clamp an out-of-range --slideshow=SECS into [0.1s,60s] (matches the runtime slider's own clamp); --fullscreen + --windowed together = last-one-wins (no clap conflict error); a NONEXISTENT positional path still errors (exit 2, stderr when console). Unknown flags / bad enum values keep clap's own exit 2. (b) EXTRAS beyond #78's set: ADD --start-at <N|name> (open at the Nth photo, 1-based, or a matching filename, instead of the first; wins over --shuffle's random start; filename match applied once the deferred scan resolves). RESERVE --new-window as a parse-accepted no-op now, so the future single-instance task #1 has its documented bypass seam and clap won't reject it later. --sort <name|date|size|random> is DEFERRED (owner: cool idea but do it as a coherent app-wide sort-order feature first, not a CLI-only bolt-on); do NOT parse-accept it yet. (c) --shuffle MECHANICS (trivial - reuses existing last_nav-steers-slideshow design, app_core_impl.rs:2550-2553 + 1054): set last_nav = Nav::Random at launch so the slideshow AND hold-to-blaze auto-advance in the precomputed random order; a DIRECTORY launch also does one random jump when the playlist resolves (start on a random photo); a SPECIFIC-FILE launch honors that file as the start (no random jump) but still sets last_nav=Random for a later slideshow. Manual Next/Prev (space/backspace) stay SEQUENTIAL and steer the slideshow back to sequential - the existing contract, matching the owner's ask (random slideshow advance + random dir-start, not random manual stepping). Flip to full mode later if wanted. (d) TDD: Cli->LaunchOverrides is a pure mapping unit-tested via Cli::try_parse_from([...]); --shuffle/--reverse/--start-at get pb-core/app-core tests. LaunchOverrides is a plain Option-field struct in pb-app-core (no clap dep); AppCore applies it, never persists. Docs: README CLI section + CHANGELOG (Added). Note: task ids were stringified by the adding commit; normalized #78 back to numeric per the tasks.json convention. (e) --reverse ADDED (owner, 2026-07-11): a direction seam over the four existing Nav variants, all routed through the launch last_nav (the slideshow + hold-to-blaze already advance via last_nav, app_core_impl.rs:1054, and toggle_slideshow does NOT reset it :5102). Mapping: neither flag=Forward, --reverse=Backward, --shuffle=Random, --shuffle+--reverse=RandomPrev (reverse shuffle - already the Shift+Enter/RandomPrev action, keymap.rs:499). Directory start position: --shuffle=random photo, --reverse=LAST photo (runway to play backward), default=first; a specific-file launch always honors the file; --start-at wins over both. Runtime discoverability stays CLI-only here - the 'tap Left/Backspace during a running slideshow to reverse' steer already works emergently (manual nav steers the slideshow) and will just be documented; a dedicated runtime reverse toggle/menu item is a possible future micro-task. (f) ARCHITECTURE REVISION (owner, 2026-07-11): macOS CLI parity is now wanted 'now-ish' (owner finishes/tests on a real Mac later), so the clap parser is extracted into a NEW shared LIB crate `pb-cli` (depends on pb-app-core + clap) instead of living inside the pb-app BINARY - a binary crate can't be a dependency, and pb-app-core must stay clap-free (NS0). pb-app depends on pb-cli; later pb-mac-ffi depends on pb-cli too and exposes one FFI entry that feeds Swift's CommandLine.arguments through the SAME parser. pb-cli is FFI-ready by design: parse_from(args-iterator) -> Result<Cli, clap::Error> with NO process::exit (help/version/errors are clap::Error kinds each shell renders itself - which also serves the Windows AttachConsole + no-console Message-dialog fallback), and argv is always a parameter (never std::env inside the lib). The render-and-exit dev commands (--hud-gallery/--egui-shot/--settings-shot + --light/--tab/--welcome) STAY intercepted in pb-app before clap (as today), so the shared Cli holds only the real cross-platform flags (+ hidden --metrics). LaunchOverrides + launch_nav + apply_to_settings already landed in pb-app-core (green, 6 tests); Nav gained Debug.

MACOS PARITY SHIPPED 2026-07-12 (subtasks 7-14; plan .taskmaster/plans/78-macos-cli-parity.md has the outcome note). #78 sits in review pending the owner live-GUI smoke listed on subtask 12.

archived.title: Text subtitles for video playback (SRT/mov_text/WebVTT) + legibility settings
archived.description:
Render text subtitles over playing video, with user-facing appearance controls (size, opacity, shadow/outline, position). Scoped to the TEXT tier only — SubRip (.srt sidecar), MP4 mov_text/tx3g, and WebVTT — decoded through the existing FFmpeg backend (task #84) and drawn with the resvg/usvg/tiny-skia text stack the HUD already uses, synced to the audio master clock. Deliberately EXCLUDES styled ASS/SSA (would want libass, a C build-risk dep this project avoids) and bitmap PGS/VobSub (separate RGBA-overlay pipeline) — log those as a stretch, don't build them. FFmpeg-backend only at first: on macOS that's MKV/WebM (+ .srt sidecars for any container); Windows MF and macOS AVFoundation get it later or route through FFmpeg. Owner's driving requirement (2026-07-13, 0.2.0 beta feedback): subtitles must be LEGIBLE and CONTROLLABLE — nothing worse than subs that fill half the screen or are unreadably small — so the appearance settings are core to this task, not a nice-to-have. Out of scope for a photo viewer's core mission, but a contained, high-value addition for anyone who actually watches films in PhotoBlaze. Cross-platform (pure-Rust text render). Split out of the 0.2.0 beta punch-list; not started this session.

=== WINDOWS CONSTRAINT (recorded 2026-07-14 by #100.8; read before starting 90.2). ===
Windows does NOT have a general-purpose FFmpeg - task #100 ships a deliberately trimmed,
demux/metadata-only build (MF still does all decode). In-container cues are fine (MP4 mov_text, MKV
subrip/ass/webvtt: demuxer + decoder both present). A STANDALONE .srt/.vtt/.ass sidecar CANNOT be
opened on Windows today: the trim enables no srt/webvtt/ass demuxer. Either widen the trim or parse
sidecars in Rust - see #100.8 for the evidence and the trade-off. Linux/macOS link a full FFmpeg and
are unaffected, so this will not reproduce off Windows.

subtasks.title: P0.8 — text-shaping spike (GATE)
subtasks.description: DONE 2026-07-14, findings in .taskmaster/docs/90-p08-text-shaping-spike.md. cosmic-text 0.19 clears the bar: shaping proven (Arabic 12 chars->11 glyphs + RTL; Devanagari 6->4 conjunct), system-font fallback finds Arabic/CJK/Devanagari/Hebrew with ZERO .notdef, RGBA8 CPU output suits both presenters, ~15-20 pure-Rust deps (harfrust, NOT rustybuzz; no C, ADR-015 clean). CORRECTION TO THE PLAN: FontSystem::new() = 261 ms / 1114 faces, so lazy-init on first subtitle use must NOT happen on the event loop -- build it on a worker (the media_details pattern) at track-select/video-open. Per-cue shape+raster = 0.15 ms mean / 0.40 ms worst warm, 1.3-1.5 ms first-use-per-script, vs an 8.3 ms frame. P0.7 presenter premise VERIFIED: NativeVideoPlayer.swift attaches AVPlayerLayer as a sublayer of the Metal canvas, so a wgpu subtitle quad would be invisible under the movie -- macOS needs a CALayer above it.

subtasks.title: Subtitle stream + sidecar discovery
subtasks.description: DONE. SidecarOrigin (pb_decode::tracks: reopenable Path | ArchiveEntry{archive,entry} -- by NAME not index, since a .srt is not a library item) + TrackLocator::Sidecar. Naming rules + encodings in pb-app-core::sidecar (20 tests, pure). PhotoSource EXTENDED with sibling_names(i)/sibling_bytes(i,name) -- the only door to a non-library file: FsSource = read_dir the parent (bare-name-only, cannot escape the dir); ZipSource = the pooled handle's central directory, scoped to the item's archive folder both ways, same decompression-bomb guards as bytes(); ScopedSource delegates through the index map; SevenZSource DELIBERATELY reports none (solid+eager: an unindexed entry's bytes were never produced, so it would need a predicate change at open or a full re-decompress per read -- pinned by a test so the gap is a decision). Discovery merges into the catalog subtitles TrackSet in media_details::probe_job, continuing the catalog id namespace so a sidecar TrackId cannot collide with an embedded stream's. Design: pure over a LIST OF SIBLING NAMES (one impl serves both sources); ENUMERATES rather than chooses (a case-collision is just two tracks); case-insensitive BY RULE so a ZIP finds the same sidecars on every host. 29 pb-source tests, Windows cross-check clean.

subtasks.title: Decode text cues to timed plain text
subtasks.description: DONE 2026-07-15. BOTH tiers ship. Sidecars: SubRip + WebVTT parsed in pure Rust (cues.rs). EMBEDDED streams: pb_decode::ffmpeg::cues (ff_stream_subtitle_cues) demuxes + avcodec_decode_subtitle2 for MKV subrip/ass/webvtt and MP4 mov_text. Lives at the `ffprobe` level, NOT beside demux.rs (which is ffvideo-gated = absent on Windows): reading a subtitle stream needs a demuxer + a SUBTITLE decoder, never a video one, so the trimmed Windows FFmpeg serves it — resolving the #100.8 constraint (sidecars stay pure-Rust and never touch FFmpeg, so Windows' missing srt/webvtt/ass DEMUXER is moot; no need to widen the trim). KEY FACT: FFmpeg normalizes EVERY text decoder's output to one ASS envelope (ff_ass_get_dialog: 8 commas then Text), so text_cue::ass_event_text (pure, tested) is the only wire-format knowledge needed. STREAMING (the design that makes it usable): reading cues is a full linear pass over the container — MEASURED 39 s on the corpus MKV (4.4 GB over SMB) — because subtitle blocks are scattered through every cluster. As a blocking wait that is indistinguishable from broken. But the reader walks in presentation order at ~70x the rate playback consumes, so it hands cues over as it finds them: MEASURED first batch at 1.06 s, 177 batches, cancellation stops a read in ~1 s not 40. CueLoad::drop cancels, so a nav can't leave a worker chewing 20 GB. FUTURE OPT: the playback demuxer already reads these packets and discards them — forwarding them would make cues cost zero I/O, but it only exists on routes using OUR demuxer, and a feature must never be gated on a backend. Layer it under, never replace. TWO ffmpeg-next LANDMINES FOUND: (1) NO Drop for Subtitle and it never calls avsubtitle_free — leaks per cue unless you free it yourself; (2) Text::get/Ass::get are from_utf8_unchecked = UB on the non-UTF-8 payloads that really exist (CP1252 .srt muxed without sub_charenc). We read the C string lossily via raw ptr instead. MOJIBAKE REPAIR (pb_app_core::mojibake, 15 tests): the corpus MKV carries `â™ª` where `♪` belongs — VERIFIED with `ffprobe -show_data` to be IN THE FILE, not our bug. Undone only when provable: re-encode a run to CP1252, require the bytes be valid UTF-8. `café` fails that (E9 is a lead with no continuation) so it is untouched. Applied per-RUN, not whole-string, at the single choke point (CueTrack::from_cues) BOTH tiers pass through. ⚠ SAFE_LEADS excludes à/á on purpose: French 'voilà «' (E0 A0 AB) IS valid UTF-8 and a naive round-trip corrupts it into a Samaritan letter — pinned by a test. Cost: mojibake'd Thai/Devanagari stays broken; the right trade. Also needed the 5 WHATWG windows-1252 passthrough bytes (0x81/8D/8F/90/9D) — `”` is E2 80 9D, so without 0x9D every CLOSING curly quote stays broken while the opening one repairs. Found by a test, not the spec.

subtasks.title: Timed overlay render + audio-clock sync
subtasks.description: PURE CORE STARTED (pb-app-core/src/subtitle.rs, 18 tests): SubtitleMode { Off, Automatic, Track(TrackId) } + resolve_track, and the placement math. OWNER DECISIONS 2026-07-14: Off means OFF (forced does NOT leak through — text on screen while the UI says off, with no way to get silence, is worse than missing a sign); Automatic = forced-only MATCHING THE AUDIO LANGUAGE (translate the signs in the film you chose; deliberately NOT system-language or OS-accessibility coupling, which would turn subtitles on by itself). Guards: a TrackId from a stale catalog generation never resolves; an unrenderable (PGS/VobSub) track never becomes active even via a stale id or Automatic; unknown audio language matches nothing (never surprise); en/eng compared through the shared display map so the backend that probed cannot change the answer. REMAINING for #90.3: the rasterizer (cosmic-text + tiny-skia -> RGBA8), Renderer::set_subtitle_overlay, the macOS SwiftUI overlay, the cue-engine clock/seek-generation wiring, and audio-clock sync. | SHIPPED: rasterizer + placement + subtitle_engine + the macOS SwiftUI presenter; clocked off AppCore::video_position() (both backends). The engine now reads the Details catalog + resolve_track (2026-07-15) — selection is real, not "the first sidecar we tripped over", and embedded tracks are reachable. REMAINING: seek generations (no stale cue flash), wire controls_h so cues lift above the transport bar.

subtasks.title: Legibility settings (the owner's core requirement)
subtasks.description: UI SHIPPED (macOS) 2026-07-15 — owner-testing. All 8 axes are reachable: a 5th Settings tab (SubtitlesPane.swift, SF `captions.bubble`) over a LIVE PREVIEW. PERSISTENCE: SubtitleStyle gained serde + a nested Settings.subtitle_style. ⚠ #[serde(default)] on SubtitleStyle AND Shadow is load-bearing, not decoration: it lives BY VALUE (unlike Option<WindowGeometry>, which is absent-or-whole), so a partial [subtitle_style] table must fill gaps from Default — otherwise a hand-edited config setting one key fails to parse, and Settings::load's 'malformed -> defaults' rule DISCARDS EVERY OTHER SETTING IN THE FILE to punish one typo here. SubtitleEngine::from_settings now takes &Settings, not a bool — post-mortem bug #2 was a preference dropped at one of its three call sites (new_host builds from defaults then re-derives); a signature that asks for the object can't be called while forgetting a field of it. THE PREVIEW (subtitle_preview.rs) is the point: 'outline 0.3%' is not a decision anyone can make from a number, and you can't see the film from inside a modal Settings window. It uses the SAME rasterizer + to_params + place() as the real overlay, so it cannot drift — that IS the one-rasterizer decision paying off. Because it uses the real place(), dragging the vertical offset negative visibly walks the text into the letterbox (the owner's headline ask, unjudgeable otherwise). Backdrop = a 2.39:1 picture (dark->light gradient + a bright band, so white text crosses a hostile patch) in the user's real letterbox colour. ⚠ LAYOUT TRAP: the preview must NOT stretch to the full pane width — a swatch WIDER than 2.39:1 pillarboxes and shows NO bars, hiding the one setting it exists to explain (a first PNG dump at 760x300 did exactly that). Capped at 420pt, 16:9. Max width + line spacing sit behind a collapsed Advanced group so the pane fits the FIXED 560x680 window. FFI: SubtitleStyleFfi is its OWN flat form, deliberately not 28 more fields on the 37-field SettingsFormFfi — the preview needs the DRAFT style every slider tick, which would mean shipping all 65 fields per frame to redraw one swatch. Font picker = a curated shortlist (owner call: fontdb finds ~1114 faces, nearly all unusable as subtitles); the stored value is a NAME, so a full picker later invalidates nothing. BUGS FOUND WHILE BUILDING: (1) TOML can hold `nan` and f32::clamp PANICS on a NaN bound while a NaN input sails through it — non-finite is reset BEFORE any clamp. (2) to_params used the raw font_family, but the FFI can't carry Option<String> and sends "" for System. (3) Color->UInt8 must clamp first: a wide-gamut pick lands outside 0...1 in sRGB and UInt8(-3.0) TRAPS in Swift. (4) the preview spinner would have spun FOREVER — nothing re-renders SwiftUI when the 261 ms font worker lands, so a .task polls until ready. REMAINING: owner verdict on the defaults ('slightly large'); the egui tab (deferred with #90.5 — the winit shell has no presenter, so it would configure an invisible feature; SettingsDraft::to_settings preserves subtitle_style untouched meanwhile).

subtasks.title: Cross-platform + backend coverage
subtasks.description: Ship on the FFmpeg backend first (macOS MKV/WebM + sidecars, all Linux). Decide the path for Windows MF and macOS AVFoundation: either add a text-cue extraction there too, or route subtitle-bearing playback through the FFmpeg backend. Verify build/run on all three. Note bitmap PGS/VobSub and styled ASS as explicit non-goals (stretch: libass behind a feature flag, PGS RGBA overlay). | The winit shell has no presenter yet (Renderer::set_subtitle_overlay) — Windows/Linux show nothing. Deferred until the style defaults settle.
subtasks.details:
WINIT PRESENTER + SETTINGS SHIPPED 2026-07-16, owner-confirmed on screen ("Subtitles do display!") against a real film over SMB. Windows now reaches parity with macOS on the two things that matter: cues DRAW and the style is CONFIGURABLE.

WHAT LANDED
1. Renderer::set_subtitle_overlay (pb-render): a sixth overlay layer. Unlike every other overlay it is placed at an ABSOLUTE origin, not an inset from an edge -- the core already placed it (subtitle::place), the renderer only converts px -> NDC. y may be slightly negative BY DESIGN (place clamps the TEXT's box, so a soft shadow bleeds off the top rather than shoving the words down); the vertex helper takes f32 for exactly that.
2. ITS OWN PREMULTIPLIED BLEND PIPELINE -- the load-bearing find. pb_hud::subtitle emits premultiplied RGBA (its own tests enforce it); the other CPU overlays are authored straight and share a pipeline whose ALPHA_BLENDING multiplies by alpha. Sending one through the other multiplies TWICE and visibly darkens every antialiased edge: measured 0.108 vs 0.216 linear. A GPU readback test (`the_subtitle_pipeline_blends_premultiplied_not_straight`) fails on exactly that mistake -- verified by pointing it at the wrong pipeline. The value it asserts is also what the macOS CGImage .premultipliedLast path produces, so the two shells match by construction rather than by eye.
3. Drawn FIRST of the overlays (pass 1b), so chrome composites above: the toast that says "Subtitles: English" shares the bottom-center strip with the cue it is talking about.
4. The presenter is SHELL-LOCAL on purpose (App::present_subtitles), NOT in tick_subtitles. macOS draws the same bitmap as a SwiftUI overlay over its AVPlayerLayer; putting this in the shared tick would draw every cue twice there. One rasterizer, two presenters.
5. POST-MORTEM BUG #2, still live in this shell, now fixed: AppCore was built by struct literal with `subtitles: Default::default()` and never called SubtitleEngine::from_settings, so `subtitles = true` on disk launched with captions OFF. Latent only because there was no presenter to reveal it. VERIFIED by trace: first tick now reports on=true.
6. Settings > Subtitles tab (egui, #90.4): all eight axes over the live preview, mirroring SubtitlesPane.swift's grouping/bounds/copy. Binds SubtitleStyle as a struct (no FFI to flatten for) and needs no debounce (the existing fold coalesces a drag). The swatch borrows the app's ONE SubtitleRasterizer -- never a second FontSystem -- and caches its texture against the exact inputs it drew.
7. The native Windows menu had NO subtitle entry AT ALL (the 'View > Subtitles' item that looked like it existed is in menu_bar_spec = the LINUX egui bar). C/Shift+C both worked and nothing said so. Added Subtitles + Next Subtitle Track to the native View menu.

TWO BUGS FOUND BY LOOKING AT THE OUTPUT (the #90 rule, paying again)
- ui.available_width() is NOT a safe texture dimension: egui's first frame reports a default screen_rect, measured 4944pt -> a 9888px texture, and egui PANICS past the GPU limit rather than clamping. Capped at the device's real max_texture_side.
- Scaled controls must write back only on .changed(): round-tripping a fraction through x100 and /100 is not bit-exact (0.04 -> 0.040000001) and the settings fold saves on ANY diff, so writing back unconditionally spews a config write every frame the tab is merely open.

REMAINING (deliberately not attempted; both are #99, not #90.5)
- The winit TRACK PICKER UI. Core is ready and shell-agnostic (subtitle_picker_rows / select_subtitle_row / subtitle_tracks_known, incl. the tri-state). Two homes, both real work: the winit 'playback bar' is a hand-laid-out egui info pill (panels_ui.rs), not a transport HStack like the Mac's, so a popover means manual layout + hit-testing + the video_bar_interactive gate; and a menu flyout needs machinery muda lacks -- macOS uses NSMenuDelegate.menuNeedsUpdate to pull tracks as the menu opens, while muda builds the tree once and only mirrors checkmarks. Shift+C + the new menu item cover the function meanwhile.
- AUDIO TRACK SWITCHING ON WINDOWS. Blocked on more than effort: WasapiAudio::open takes no track at all, and the catalog hands out TrackLocator::FfStream (an FFMPEG stream index, since #100 made FFmpeg the demuxer) while MF's Source Reader enumerates its OWN indices -- a real currency mismatch the TrackLocator seam exists for but nobody has resolved. On top of that, Windows audio IS the master clock, so a mid-playback switch must tear down and re-prime it at the playhead (main.rs already documents this as the genuinely hard half). And it cannot be verified without listening. Left alone.

LINUX: unverified. Same wgpu path, so it should follow, but nobody has run it.

archived.details: STATUS 2026-07-16: subtasks 3 and 4 shipped + owner-verified on macOS. Subtask 5 (the winit presenter + the egui Settings tab + the Windows menu) shipped and is owner-confirmed displaying on Windows; it is in REVIEW pending the owner's pass over the tab and the defaults. Linux is unverified (same wgpu path). What is left is #99 work, not #90: the winit track-picker UI, and Windows audio-track switching (blocked on an FFmpeg-vs-MediaFoundation stream-index mismatch plus the master-clock re-prime).

archived.title: Stuck preview: full-res never upgrades in the normal flow (blurry in Fit / tiny in 1:1)
archived.description:
Owner-reported 2026-07-18, reproduces on a plain SSD FOLDER too (so NOT archive-specific; an archive only widens the timing window). Sometimes loading a photo shows the low-res EXIF preview and it NEVER sharpens until a resize / fullscreen toggle / scale change forces a fresh decode. The unifying clue: pressing 0 (1:1/Original mode) in that state SHRINKS the image to the PREVIEW's native size — proving both symptoms are ONE root: the full-resolution decode is stuck at the preview stage (preview shown; full upgrade never completes). In Fit mode → upscaled/blurry; in Original mode → the tiny preview at true 1:1. A resize re-decodes fresh and completes.
NOT the surface-drop bug (the preview IS presented; it's the full that's missing) — distinct from the frozen-door / same-size-Lost surface issue (that one still needs surface recreation, held in reserve).
Candidate mechanisms traced (app_core_impl.rs, verify with a diagnostic — DON'T guess): sharpen_now (~5653) only requests the full while display_slot(d).is_some() && preview_resident.contains(d) && !upgrade_done.contains(d); request_prefetch (~5497) SKIPS the sharpen when `resident && !is_prev` ('already full'). So a preview that's resident-but-not-in-preview_resident, or shown via the single-image path (load_current_sync ~6814 uses set_image, outside the ring, so display_slot is None), or a full outcome dropped in drain_results' retain (~6611: kept only if `is_prev && !img.is_preview`; else dropped and possibly upgrade_done'd) — any of these leaves the preview stranded. Cancellation is cleanly discarded (decode_pool ~388/417), so it's NOT that. upgrade_done (~6471/6611) is the permanent 'stop sharpening' flag — a genuine decode error OR a full-that-came-back-a-preview sets it.
NEXT: add a gated preview->full lifecycle diagnostic (preview presented / sharpen requested / full landed: is_preview, is_prev, kept|dropped|upgrade_done) so ONE capture pins which path strands it, then fix. Likely a pre-existing #106.5/#106.7 interaction, not the recent mip/resize work.

archived.title: Smoother hold-to-pan / hold-to-zoom — gentler acceleration curve
archived.description: Owner feel note (2026-07-09): holding the pan/zoom keys accelerates too aggressively and doesn't feel smooth — want a slower, gentler ramp with smoother motion. The hold-to-view loop is AppCore::apply_view_holds (crates/pb-app-core/src/app_core_impl.rs:5642), driven by the tuning constants in crates/pb-app-core/src/engine.rs: zoom e-folding rate ramps ZOOM_MIN_RATE 0.5 -> ZOOM_MAX_RATE 2.5 over ZOOM_RAMP_SECS 0.7 (exp() applied multiplicatively about center); pan speed ramps PAN_MIN_SPEED 450 -> PAN_MAX_SPEED 3200 px/s over PAN_RAMP_SECS 0.7. Both are already time-based (frame-rate independent, dt-clamped to 0.1s) so 'smoother' here means the FEEL of the ramp, not a timing bug. Two levers: (a) TUNING — lower the max rate/speed and/or lengthen the ramp so it starts and stays gentler (e.g. PAN_MAX ~1800-2400, ZOOM_MAX ~1.5-2.0, RAMP ~1.0-1.2s), a one-file constant change; (b) CURVE SHAPE — the ramp is currently LINEAR in t (min + (max-min)*(t/ramp)); an ease-in (smoothstep / t^2) keeps fine control longer at the start before building speed, which reads as 'smoother'. Optional stretch: a short release ease-out / inertia so motion doesn't stop dead on key-up. Shared-core feel change (helps macOS + Linux too), surfaced while testing on Windows; keep it a measured, owner-in-the-loop tuning pass, not a blind edit.
archived.details: Scope options, cheapest first: (1) Retune the six constants (ZOOM_MIN/MAX_RATE, ZOOM_RAMP_SECS, PAN_MIN/MAX_SPEED, PAN_RAMP_SECS) for a gentler start and lower top speed — pure constant edit in engine.rs, no logic change. (2) Swap the linear ramp for an ease-in in apply_view_holds: factor the shared 'min + (max-min) * shape(t/ramp)' into a small pure helper (e.g. ease_in(u)=u*u or smoothstep) so zoom and pan share one curve and it's unit-testable (assert monotonic, ease_in(0)=0, ease_in(1)=1, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Keep the multiplicative exp() zoom-about-center and the pan clamp untouched. (3) Optional inertia: on key release, decay the last velocity over ~150-250ms instead of zeroing zoom_started/pan_started immediately — bigger change, own subtask, only if the owner still wants more polish after (1)+(2). Note the scroll-wheel/trackpad steps (WHEEL_ZOOM_STEP, PIXEL_ZOOM_STEP, WHEEL_PAN_STEP, PINCH_GAIN) are a SEPARATE input path (AppCore::scroll, not apply_view_holds) — the owner's note is about held-key motion, so leave the gesture constants unless they ask. Prime directive: this is off the photo hot path (only runs while a pan/zoom key is held), so feel is free to change; still no per-frame heap alloc. Consider whether any of these should become settings (nav ramp/start/max are already configurable) vs hard-coded; default to constants unless the owner wants a knob.
archived.testStrategy: Primarily owner feel-test on device (Windows first, then confirm macOS/Linux unchanged-for-the-better): hold each pan direction and zoom in/out, confirm the start is gentle enough for fine framing and the top speed is comfortable, not lurchy. If the ramp is refactored into a pure ease helper, unit-test the curve (endpoints, monotonicity, gentler-than-linear midpoint). Regression: apply_view_holds still returns changed=true only while keys are held (loop keeps polling) and pan stays clamped to image bounds; keypress->photon nav timing is untouched (this path is nav-independent).
